LEAF & LINEAGE · RELEASE 20261022-18

Lift, spring, puff: test results

7,200 simulated matches: nine controlled builds, 36 pairings, 100 decision seeds, and both corner orders per seed. Each beetle has 1,600 matches. Numeric base traits start at their midpoint and growth modifiers at zero; listed modifications are the only differences. This is an invented teaching model, not real beetle biology. No KO or health meter is used.

Single-specialist win rates against the midpoint build were 58.5% for the long-horn lifter, 45.5% for the jumper and 42% for the puffer. The combined build won 43%. More moves do not ensure victory: poor timing and unnecessary attempts spend energy and positioning. These results cover a finite fixture set with unequal trait investment; they do not prove universal balance. The coordinated build was strongest in this sample, so classroom observations can still guide future tuning.

Other verification

187 automated tests passed, including gradual inheritance of all eighteen new factors, rare recessive expression, rare founder prevalence, bounded mutation jumps, lifts versus positioning and grip, airborne contact/dodges, puff charges/range, cooldowns, instincts, old SUMO5 replay identity, exact two-screen 10× simulation, saved match validation and archived portraits. Live service tests confirmed anonymous packets, private tables, capability checks, mismatch rejection, exact adaptation genes and trade receipts.
